title: Part Time Payroll Assistant
company: Adele Carr Recruitment Limited - Agency - Permanent
description:
Part-Time Payroll Assistant

Location: Northwich
Salary: Competitive, dependent on experience
Job Type: Permanent, Part-Time
Hours: 15 or 22.5 hours per week, over 2 or 3 days

We are currently recruiting for a Part-Time Payroll Assistant to join an established and growing professional services business in Northwich.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who already has some payroll experience and is looking to broaden their knowledge, take on more responsibility and develop their career within payroll. You'll join a supportive and experienced payroll team, with plenty of opportunity to learn and develop your skills across a varied client base.

The Role

Working as part of the payroll team, you will assist with the accurate and timely processing of payrolls for a diverse portfolio of clients. This will include weekly, fortnightly, four-weekly and monthly payrolls for sole traders, partnerships and limited companies across a range of sectors.

You will work closely with experienced payroll professionals, giving you the opportunity to develop your technical knowledge, gain exposure to different payroll requirements and build your confidence in dealing with clients and payroll queries.

Key Responsibilities
- Assist with the preparation and processing of payrolls for a portfolio of clients.
- Process payroll information accurately and ensure deadlines are met.
- Support with payroll administration, including Auto Enrolment and BACS processing.
- Respond to routine payroll queries from clients, colleagues, HMRC and other third parties.
- Maintain accurate and up-to-date payroll records.
- Assist with resolving payroll issues and escalate more complex queries when required.
- Keep up to date with payroll legislation and statutory requirements.
- Build strong and professional relationships with clients.
- Work collaboratively with the wider payroll team.
- Contribute to improving payroll processes and delivering a high level of client service.

About You

We're looking for someone with some previous payroll experience who is keen to develop and expand their skill set.

You will ideally have:
- Previous experience working in a payroll role.
- A good understanding of basic payroll processes and statutory requirements.
- Some knowledge of Auto Enrolment and statutory payments.
- Experience using payroll software; BrightPay experience would be advantageous but is not essential.
- Good attention to detail and a high level of accuracy.
- Strong organisational and time-management skills.
- Good communication skills and a professional, client-focused approach.
- The ability to work independently while also being a strong team player.
- A positive attitude and genuine interest in developing a career in payroll.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and Outlook.

Experience within a payroll bureau or accountancy practice would be advantageous, but candidates from an in-house payroll background will also be considered.

Why Join?

You'll be joining a supportive team where you can continue to develop your payroll experience while working with a varied client portfolio. The role offers flexibility and could suit someone looking to balance their career with other commitments.

Benefits include:
- 36 days' holiday including Bank Holidays and Christmas period (full-time equivalent)
- 5% employer pension contribution
- Option to buy or sell up to 5 days' holiday
- Employee Assistance Programme
- Life Assurance
- Enhanced maternity, paternity and shared parental pay
- Enhanced sick pay
- Referral scheme
- Paid volunteer time
- Long-service enhancements to pension contributions and holiday entitlement
- On-site parking
- Team social events
- Free fruit

Hours & Flexibility

This is a permanent part-time position, with flexibility around working hours.

Applications are welcomed from candidates looking to work either:
- 15 hours per week over 2 days, or
- 22.5 hours per week over 3 days

title: Payroll & Finance Officer
description:
Payroll & Finance Officer

Salary: £32,000 - £35,000

Location: Remote - Cheshire

Working Setup: Remote, with very occasional travel to the
Cheshire office

Contract: Permanent

Hours: Full-time

JGA Recruitment Group are working exclusively with a growing
education organisation to recruit a Payroll & Finance Officer
into their central team.

This is a fantastic opportunity for an experienced payroll
professional who enjoys working independently and wants to take
ownership of an in-house payroll function supporting multiple
schools.

The role is currently approximately 75% payroll and 25% finance,
with the payroll element expected to increase as the organisation
continues to grow. You will be responsible for the accurate and
timely processing of payroll across academies and a central team.

The Role

Reporting to the Finance Manager, you will take ownership of the
day-to-day payroll operation, ensuring employees are paid
accurately and on time while managing payroll-related pensions,
statutory submissions and stakeholder queries.

Alongside payroll, you will support the wider finance team with
reconciliations, invoices, month-end activity and general
financial administration.

The role is predominantly remote, with occasional travel to the
Cheshire office - approximately once a month during term time -
so candidates within a reasonable commuting distance of Cheshire
are preferred.

Key Responsibilities

Manage the end-to-end monthly payroll for multiple academies
and the central team.
Ensure payroll calculations, deductions and submissions are
accurate and completed within agreed deadlines.
Manage payroll-related queries and liaise with employees,
schools, senior stakeholders and external bodies including HMRC
and pension providers.
Manage Teachers' Pensions and Local Government Pension Scheme
requirements, including relevant forms, returns and deductions.
Complete monthly payroll and budget reconciliations,
investigating and explaining variances.
Upload monthly payroll costs to the finance system and support
the wider finance team with reporting and administration.
Review and approve academy invoices and assist with month-end
routines.
Support bank reconciliations, the asset register and wider
financial administration.
Provide advice and guidance to colleagues on payroll and
finance matters.
Identify opportunities to improve payroll and finance processes
as the organisation continues to grow.

About You

The successful candidate will have:

Current or recent experience running a monthly payroll from end
to end.
Previous education, academy or school payroll experience is
highly desirable.
A strong understanding of PAYE, pensions and UK payroll
legislation.
Experience with Teachers' Pensions and/or LGPS would be
advantageous.
Experience using payroll software
AAT qualification or equivalent experience, with an
understanding of accruals-based accounting.
Good Excel and wider MS Office skills.
Strong attention to detail and the ability to work accurately
to tight payroll deadlines.
The confidence to work independently, manage your own workload
and take ownership of the payroll function.
Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain
payroll and financial information clearly to non-finance
colleagues.

What's on Offer

£32,000 - £35,000 salary
Permanent position
Predominantly remote working
Occasional travel to the Cheshire office during term time
5 weeks' annual leave, increasing to 6 weeks after 5 years'
service
Bank holidays
Local Government Pension Scheme
Individualised, funded training plan
Annual flu jab
Cycle to Work Scheme
Opportunity to develop with a growing organisation and take
increasing ownership of the payroll function

Interested?

If you're an experienced payroll professional with
education-sector experience and are looking for a predominantly
remote role where you can take genuine ownership of the payroll
function, we'd love to hear from you.

Privacy Notice

JGA Recruitment Group Ltd ("We") are committed to equality of
opportunity for all applications regardless of age, disability,
, gender reassignment, sexual orientation, pregnancy and
maternity, race, religion or belief, and marriage and civil
partnerships. We strongly encourage suitably qualified applicants
from a wide range of backgrounds to apply.

We are also committed to protecting and respecting your privacy.
We are a specialist Payroll and HR recruitment agency and
recruitment business as defined in the Employment Agencies and
Employment Businesses Regulations 2003.

title: Purchase Ledger Assistant
description:
Purchase Ledger Assistant

Location: Winsford

Job Type: Full time, permanent

Salary: £25,000-£30,000 depending on experience

HRGO Recruitment are recruiting a Purchase Ledger Assistant to join a busy finance team.

Working as part of the wider finance function, you will help ensure supplier accounts are accurately maintained, invoices and payments are processed efficiently, and any queries or discrepancies are resolved promptly.

The role:
- Maintain accurate and up to date purchase ledger records, ensuring invoices and accounts payable information are processed correctly.
- Reconcile supplier statements against internal records and investigate and resolve any discrepancies.
- Monitor the Goods Received Not Invoiced account, following up outstanding purchase orders, receipts and unmatched invoices.
- Process supplier payments accurately and within agreed deadlines.
- Respond to purchase ledger and supplier queries, working closely with internal departments and external contacts to resolve issues.
- Produce regular finance reports, including weekly and monthly reporting for management.
- Provide general administrative support to the finance team, including handling incoming calls and responding to routine finance-related enquiries.
- Assist with other finance and administrative activities as required.

The candidate:
- Previous experience in a Purchase Ledger, Accounts Payable or a similar finance role is required.
- A good understanding of the purchase-to-pay process, including purchase order matching and supplier statement reconciliation.
- AAT qualification or current AAT study, ideally at Level 2 or above, is desirable.
- Experience using an ERP or cloud based accounting system
- Excellent attention to detail and a methodical approach to financial administration.
- Strong communication skills and the confidence to deal professionally with suppliers and internal stakeholders.
- Good organisational and time management skills, with the ability to prioritise competing deadlines in a busy environment.
- The ability to work accurately within a high volume, largely paperless finance environment.

For further information, please contact Sophie on or email
